To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have found a new method of perturbative expansion, and have applied it successfully to several models of cosmological density and gravitational fields.

(1) the nonlinear gravitational evolution of the cosmological density field can be expressed as a perturbation series in the initial density field, (2) the nonlinear gravitational velocity field can also be expressed as a similar perturbation series in terms of the initial velocity field, (3) the higher-order terms in the perturbation series are given in terms of the lower-order terms, (4) the perturbation series for the density and velocity fields can be applied to the analytically integratable models

we have derived an analytic formula for the perturbative solution of the nonlinear gravitational field equation in the Universe, and have applied the result to several analytially integrable models whose initial linear power spectra obey a power law, and approach that predicted by the cold-dark-mater scenario.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the perturbation theory of nonlinear gravitational evolution of the cosmological density field, with the aim of understanding its dependence on the linear power spectrum.
the nonlinear gravitational evolution of cosmological density and peculiar velocity fields.
the nonlinear gravitational evolution in cosmology.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in a universe with cold dark matter, the nonlinear gravitational evolution can be calculated in a closed form for any initial power spectrum.

the perturbation expansion of the nonlinear gravitational evolution of the cosmological density and the velocity fields can be systematically performed in terms of the initial spectrum, which is a function of the Fourier wave-number.
the nonlinear evolution of the gravitational fields can be calculated in a systematic way, and the results can be applied to the analysis of the large-scale structure of the Universe.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nonlinear gravitational evolution is not universal, and depends on the initial spectrum.

the perturbation theory of nonlinear gravitational fields is analytically tractable and can be used to study the nonlinear evolution of cosmological density and peculiar velocity fields in the Universe.
the nonlinear evolution of the fields is a function of the linear power spectrum and the initial conditions only, and not of any other cosmological parameters.
